headline: COPPER TARIFFS LOCKED IN — JUNE 30 COMMERCE REPORT SEALS PHASED DUTY PATH; COMEX HITS RECORD 650,000T, GOLDMAN EYES $14,000/T
snippet: The U.S. Commerce Department's Section 232 national-security report on copper, delivered to the White House on June 30, 2026, recommended a phased schedule of refined copper import tariffs — 15% effective January 2027, rising to 30% January 2028 — triggering a structural divergence between COMEX and LME that has driven COMEX copper inventories to a record 650,000-plus tonnes (from approximately 80,000 tonnes at the start of 2026) as traders rush to pre-position domestic supply ahead of the duty ramp. Goldman Sachs, citing the tariff timeline alongside three simultaneous mine supply shocks (Grasberg mudslide, Kamoa acid shortage, Chile -9% year-on-year), maintained a copper price target above US$14,000 per tonne and argued that the COMEX/LME spread effectively prices the tariff regime before it formally takes effect.

headline: FREEMAN GOLD LEMHI DELIVERS $696M POST-TAX NPV AND 34.4% IRR — STOCK JUMPS 20% ON MAIDEN FEASIBILITY STUDY (TSXV:FMAN)
source_name: Canadian Mining Journal / Freeman Gold Corp.
snippet: Freeman Gold Corp. (TSXV:FMAN) published its maiden Feasibility Study for the Lemhi Gold Project in Idaho on June 29, 2026, delivering a US$696 million after-tax NPV5% and a 34.4% IRR at a US$3,650/oz base-case gold price — with a 15-year open-pit mine life, a 2.5-year capital payback, and an AISC of US$1,719/oz across a Proven and Probable reserve of 1.03 million gold ounces. The study tripled the project's independently assessed value from the prior PEA, supported by a 47% improvement in recoveries through optimised processing, and Freeman Gold shares jumped approximately 20% on the announcement. The FS advances Lemhi — a permitted, road-accessible heap-leach project in the prolific Salmon River Mountains — to construction-readiness at a gold price that remains 9% below the June 30, 2026 spot price of approximately US$4,000.

headline: JP MORGAN JUNE 30: FED TURNS GOLD PAUSE INTO "DEEPER FREEZE" — COPPER AND MINE SUPPLY THE BETTER H2 2026 THESIS
snippet: J.P. Morgan's June 30, 2026 mid-year metals outlook — published via Kitco News — argues that the Federal Reserve's pause narrative has been captured by Kevin Warsh's hawkish recalibration, turning what should have been a structural gold tailwind into a "very large lack of engagement" in the gold market as rate-hike risk priced for September keeps institutional buyers sidelined. The bank directed clients toward copper for H2 2026, citing mine supply as "very anemic" against demand growth from data centres, grid investment, and electrification — and noting that the COMEX/LME copper spread created by Section 232 tariff pre-positioning has structurally improved the economics of North American copper projects relative to global peers. J.P. Morgan maintained its Q4 2026 gold average target at US$6,000/oz, implying the bank views the current sub-$4,000 print as a cyclical low, not a structural reversal.

headline: SAGA METALS DOUBLES DRILL RATE TO 400m/DAY AT RADAR TITANIUM-VANADIUM — MRE TECHNICAL REPORT ON TRACK FOR LATE 2026 (TSXV:SAGA)
snippet: SAGA Metals Corp. (TSXV:SAGA) announced June 29, 2026 the deployment of a second diamond drill rig at its Radar Titanium-Vanadium Project in Labrador, doubling on-site drilling capacity to 400 metres per day, following completion of 13,149 metres across 61-plus holes confirming continuous VTM (vanadium-titanium magnetite) and ilmenite mineralisation across a large-footprint deposit. Oxide zones up to 224 metres thick have returned grades of more than 45–58% Fe₂O₃, 6–8% TiO₂, and 0.37–0.44% V₂O₅ across multiple drill fences; a NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate technical report is targeted for late 2026. Radar is emerging as one of the largest undeveloped titanium-vanadium resources in North America at a time when vanadium's energy-storage and defence applications are generating new investor interest independent of the traditional steel-alloy demand channel.

headline: URANIUM SPOT HITS 7-MONTH HIGH $79/LB ON JUNE 27 — SPROTT REPORTS INVESTOR CONVICTION AS KAZATOMPROM CUTS QUOTA TO 77M lbs
snippet: Sprott Asset Management's July 2026 monthly uranium commentary reports that spot U₃O₈ hit a seven-month high of US$79 per pound on June 27 before settling near US$78.50 at month-end — a 9.7% rise from May's US$71.55 close — as Kazatomprom announced a reduction in its 2026 production quota from 85 million pounds to 77 million pounds, removing meaningful near-term supply from the world's largest uranium producer. The Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index rose 17.01% in June, with the junior miner sub-index gaining 21.75%, as Sprott argues investors are "acting with conviction" by accumulating physical uranium and producer equities at levels that price in neither the quota cut nor the accelerating global reactor build-out that makes the 2027–2032 supply gap structurally unresolvable without new mine production currently unfinanced.

headline: STONEX GOLD H2 2026: SEASONAL TROUGH MAY EXTEND TO SEPTEMBER — REAL RATES AND DOLLAR ARE THE ONLY CIRCUIT BREAKERS
snippet: StoneX head of market analysis Rhona O'Connell's H2 2026 gold outlook, published around July 1, 2026, argues that the seasonal trough that historically falls in late July may extend by four to six weeks — potentially into September — because the Fed hawkishness driving the current correction adds a monetary headwind on top of the usual summer demand lull. O'Connell identifies two circuit breakers: a soft PCE print below 3.4% that reduces the September rate-hike probability (shifting real rates lower without a Fed meeting), or a geopolitical escalation that revives safe-haven demand above the macro-rate channel. In the base case — no circuit breaker and a September hike priced at 60%-plus odds — gold could test the US$3,800–3,850 zone before the historically reliable Q4 recovery begins, with the dollar at a one-year high and real 10-year yields still positive functioning as a ceiling on price recovery until one of the two triggers materialises.
